subsystems.name: Neutrino source
subsystems.role: creates a directed, very intense neutrino beam.
parts: target and magnetic horns to focus pions
decay tunnel where pions decay into muons and neutrinos

subsystems.name: Beam modulation
subsystems.role: imposes a pattern of ones and zeros on the beam.
parts: fast pulsing or steering of the proton beam

subsystems.name: Beam path
subsystems.role: aims the neutrinos through whatever matter is in the way — rock, ocean or a planet.
parts: negligible attenuation loss in the rock itself

subsystems.name: Detector array
subsystems.role: catches the vanishingly rare interactions that carry the message.
parts: thousands of tonnes of liquid argon, water Cherenkov or liquid scintillator
deep underground cavity or naturally shielded site

subsystems.name: Readout and decoding
subsystems.role: turns few detected events into symbols.

buildSteps.title: Build the accelerator
buildSteps.detail: A high-power proton synchrotron or linac, rated in megawatts, provides the primary beam; this is the single largest cost.

buildSteps.title: Make a neutrino beam
buildSteps.detail: Protons strike a target, magnetic horns focus the resulting pions, and a long decay tunnel converts them into a collimated neutrino beam.

buildSteps.title: Add modulation hardware
buildSteps.detail: Fast kicker magnets or beam choppers switch the proton beam on and off, or shift its direction slightly, on a controlled clock — this carries the bits.

buildSteps.title: Choose the receiver site
buildSteps.detail: A detector large enough to catch a usable event rate is placed hundreds to thousands of kilometres away, with an independent timing link to the transmitter.

buildSteps.title: Build the detector
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of tonnes of active medium are instrumented with photodetectors in an underground cavity so cosmic rays do not swamp the signal.

buildSteps.title: Synchronise and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Fine clocks and known beam pulses align transmitter and receiver, and calibration runs establish the background rate.

buildSteps.title: Send and decode
buildSteps.detail: Each symbol is repeated over many accelerator pulses so it can be distinguished statistically from background; software integrates the data into reconstructed bits.

prerequisites.why: detectable neutrino rates demand beam powers far beyond early experiments.
experiments such as MINERvA, IceCube and DUNE-class detectors exist or are being built, but a communication receiver needs even more mass and quiet.
switching a megawatt beam at useful data rates is harder than the slow on/off used in demonstrations.
transmitter and receiver must agree on when each symbol was sent, often across interplanetary distances.

prerequisites.tech: Feasible error-correction coding for event rates of a few counts per second
prerequisites.why: the detected signal is so sparse that conventional coding schemes do not apply.

pathway.milestone: 1950s–2000s: the idea that a neutrino beam could penetrate the Earth essentially unattenuated and be read by a huge detector
pathway.unlocks: a communication channel with no line-of-sight requirement.

pathway.milestone: 2012: a Fermilab experiment (using the NuMI beam and the MINERvA detector) sent the word for the particle itself through hundreds of metres of rock
pathway.unlocks: proof that neutrino messaging is physically possible — at a rate of a few bits per second at best and needing many pulses per symbol.

pathway.milestone: purpose-built experiments pushing rate and detector mass, such as a dedicated modulation test with a large liquid-argon receiver
pathway.unlocks: realistic link budgets for long-distance links.

pathway.milestone: one-way signalling to deep submarines or spacecraft, or a clock-synchronisation beacon
pathway.unlocks: communication paths no radio or optical link can reach — only if accelerator power and detector cost fall drastically.
